source: Shi et al. (2023) Large Language Models Can Be Easily Distracted by Irrelevant Context
finding: Adding one irrelevant sentence to grade-school math problems sharply lowers model accuracy. This is the machine version of 'surface features capture the novice'.
numbers: GSM-IC, 4,000-problem sample (GSM-IC-4K), code-davinci-002 and text-davinci-003. Fewer than 30% of base problems were solved consistently (macro accuracy) after distractors were added.
limits: 2022-era GPT-3 models; later models are more robust, but see GSM-NoOp (c03).
agent_relevance: Strong evidence that a model keyed on surface cues needs an explicit representation step that separates relevant from irrelevant quantities (S2).

source: Shi et al. (2023) GSM-IC: mitigations
finding: Three fixes work: self-consistency, distractor-bearing exemplars, and the instruction to ignore irrelevant information. Plain 'Solve grade school math problems' does not help; the ignore-clause is what matters.
numbers: Self-consistency (20 samples) raised overall micro accuracy by more than 11 points. Least-to-most roughly doubled macro accuracy versus COT on code-davinci-002 but not on text-davinci-003. No accuracy loss on clean GSM8K from these fixes.
quote: Feel free to ignore irrelevant information given in the questions.
limits: Role-overlap distractors made text-davinci-003 macro accuracy fall to 0 on problems with more than 2 steps.
agent_relevance: A cheap representation-time instruction (name what is irrelevant) is a candidate S2 element; test at equal tokens (G7).

source: Mirzadeh et al. (2025, ICLR) GSM-Symbolic: Understanding the Limitations of Mathematical Reasoning in LLMs
finding: Adding one clause that looks relevant but is not (GSM-NoOp) causes large drops, even for o1-preview. Models turn statements into operations without grasping meaning (for example, any 'discount' becomes multiply).
numbers: GSM-NoOp: drops of up to 65% (Phi-3-mini over 65%); o1-preview -17.5%, Gemma-7b-it -20.6%, Mistral-7b-v0.3 -24.0%. 8 shots of the same question with the irrelevant clause did not fix it (within one SD).
limits: Authors read this as pattern matching; that is an interpretation, not a tested mechanism. Greedy decoding except o1 models.
agent_relevance: Direct modern test of surface cue triggers wrong operation. Argues for a represent step that checks each quantity's role before computing.

source: Mirzadeh et al. (2025) GSM-Symbolic: number changes and clause count
finding: Changing only numbers lowers accuracy and raises variance across instances of the same template. Original GSM8K scores often sit on the right tail of the GSM-Symbolic distribution.
numbers: More than 20 open models (2B-27B) plus GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o, o1-mini, o1-preview. Performance fell and variance rose with each added clause (GSM-P1, GSM-P2).
limits: Template-based variants may differ from natural variation.
agent_relevance: Any measurement of our agent should use symbolic variants of items, not single fixed items.

source: Zheng et al. (2023) Take a Step Back: Evoking Reasoning via Abstraction in LLMs
finding: Asking first for the principles or concepts behind a problem, then reasoning from them, lifts accuracy on physics. This is the closest prompt analogue of an expert's principle-based categorisation.
numbers: MMLU high-school Physics: PaLM-2L 66.4% baseline vs 73.2% step-back (CoT 65%); GPT-4 69.4% vs 84.5% (CoT 82.9%); Llama2-70B 51.9% vs 64.8% (CoT 59.3%). Chemistry: PaLM-2L 70.9% vs 81.8%; GPT-4 80.9% vs 85.6%; Llama2-70B 55.7% vs 66.7%. 5 runs each.
limits: For GPT-4 on Physics, CoT already reached 82.9%, so the extra gain from step-back is small there. Few-shot demonstrations used. The headline gain of up to 36% is from other tasks.
agent_relevance: Candidate S2 operator: state the governing principle before solving. Gain is largest where the baseline is weak.

source: Zheng et al. (2023) Step-Back error analysis
finding: The abstraction step rarely fails; the reasoning step after it is the bottleneck. Step-back fixes some errors and creates some.
numbers: On MMLU Physics, step-back corrected 20.5% of baseline errors and introduced 11.9% new errors. Over 90% of remaining errors were in the reasoning step; principle errors were a small fraction.
limits: Error labels assigned in the paper's own analysis; few exemplars sufficed to teach abstraction.
agent_relevance: Naming the right principle is easy for a model; applying it is hard. A verifier (code, G3) is needed after S2.

source: Zheng et al. (2023) Step-Back on knowledge-heavy tasks
finding: On TimeQA baselines were low and CoT or take-a-deep-breath gave no gain; step-back (with retrieval) gave large gains.
numbers: TimeQA baseline GPT-4 45.6%, PaLM-2L 41.5%. MuSiQue and StrategyQA tested with the same protocol.
limits: Retrieval-augmented; not a pure representation effect.
agent_relevance: An abstraction question also helps retrieve the right facts, a second route to the same benefit.

source: Didolkar et al. (2024) Metacognitive Capabilities of LLMs: An Exploration in Mathematical Problem Solving
finding: GPT-4 can label math questions by the skill needed and cluster labels into interpretable families. Using those labels to pick in-context examples beats topic-based or random choice. A working machine version of classify by deep structure.
numbers: MATH, GPT-4-0613: skill-based exemplars +11.6% over standard CoT, +3.5% over Complex CoT, +3.5% over topic-based. Code-based (PAL) variant +7.52% over PAL baseline. Skills from GPT-4 also helped Mixtral 8x7B and transferred from GSM8K to other word-problem sets.
limits: Needs a strong labeller (GPT-4). Examples labelled on training sets, so a pre-built repository is required.
agent_relevance: Strongest direct evidence for S2: represent a problem by its skill or principle label, then retrieve by that label rather than by wording.

source: Didolkar et al. (2024): fine-grained versus coarse categories
finding: Fine skill labels beat coarse topic labels. Complexity of examples is not a good proxy for relevance.
numbers: Skill-based beat Topic-Based by 3.5 points and Complex CoT by 3.5 points on MATH. With self-consistency, skill exemplars scored highest in 4 of 6 transfer cases, +4.0% over CoT+SC in one.
limits: Single lab, single main model; no human-expert comparison of the label sets.
agent_relevance: Granularity matters: topic (algebra) is the novice level, skill is closer to the expert level in Chi et al.

source: Yasunaga et al. (2023) Large Language Models as Analogical Reasoners
finding: Asking the model to recall relevant solved problems of its own before solving works without labelled exemplars. The gain is notable on MATH, where problem types vary.
numbers: Codeforces Level-A (Jan-Aug 2023): GPT-3.5-turbo-16k Acc@1 rose from 8% (0-shot) to 15% with self-generated exemplars plus knowledge; GPT-4 16% to 17%. GPT-3.5 with the method (15%) was close to GPT-4 baseline (16%).
limits: Self-generated exemplars can be wrong. Exact GSM8K and MATH cells were not cleanly extracted from the PDF text.
agent_relevance: Self-recall of same-structure problems is a representation-time operator; compare with retrieval by label (c08).

source: Deng et al. (2024) Rephrase and Respond: Let LLMs Ask Better Questions for Themselves
finding: Having the model rewrite the question in its own words before answering lifts GPT-4 on many tasks. The model's frame differs from the human's frame.
numbers: 10 tasks, GPT-4. Last-letter concatenation rose to almost 100%. Larger gains for GPT-4 than for GPT-3.5 or Vicuna-13b. On CSQA, where the question is clear, gain was marginal.
limits: Gains largest where the original question is ambiguous. Rephrasings can drift in meaning.
agent_relevance: Restating the problem (S2) helps most when the stated problem is poorly formed; do not apply by default (G1, G7).

source: Xu et al. (2024) Re-Reading Improves Reasoning in LLMs (RE2)
finding: Repeating the question in the prompt gives small, consistent gains. Not a deep-structure effect; it works through attention.
numbers: 14 datasets, 112 experiments. davinci-003 Vanilla+RE2 average gains: arithmetic +3.81, commonsense +2.51, symbolic +1.85. With CoT: +2.22, +1.23, +5.25.
limits: Gains small; exceptions on vanilla ChatGPT. Doubles question length.
agent_relevance: A cheap, weak baseline. Any S2 claim should beat re-reading at equal tokens.

source: Zhou et al. (2024) Self-Discover: LLMs Self-Compose Reasoning Structures
finding: The model picks reasoning modules and composes one structure per task type, then reuses it for all instances. Gains over CoT on 21 of 25 tasks.
numbers: BBH, T4D, MATH. Gains up to 42%; on one model average BBH +11%, T4D +39%, MATH +5.5%. Beats CoT-Self-Consistency by over 20% with 10-40x less inference compute.
limits: Structure is chosen per task, not per instance. Best on world-knowledge tasks, moderate on algorithmic ones.
agent_relevance: Shows that a per-task-type structure is cheap, made once, and can be cached.

source: Yang et al. (2024) Buffer of Thoughts: Thought-Augmented Reasoning with LLMs
finding: A Problem Distiller extracts key variables and constraints, then a template library is searched by that distilled form. Disabling the distiller lowers accuracy, more so on hard problems.
numbers: 10 tasks, GPT-4: +11% Game of 24, +20% Geometric Shapes, +51% Checkmate-in-One over Meta-prompting; 12% of the cost of multi-query methods; Llama3-8B+BoT may beat Llama3-70B. Distiller ablation: bigger drops on Game of 24 and Checkmate than on word sorting and MGSM.
limits: Authors' own benchmarks and ablation; exact ablation values not extracted here. Template reuse can hit a poor match.
agent_relevance: A direct agent-loop implementation of represent, then retrieve by structure. Closest to our S2 plus a case store.

source: Hong et al. (2024) Abstraction-of-Thought Makes Language Models Better Reasoners
finding: Fine-tuning on reasoning that goes abstract first, then concrete, beats CoT-format fine-tuning on unseen BIG-Bench Hard tasks. The format itself is the cause.
numbers: 348k-sample AoT Collection; 23 unseen BBH tasks. AoT beat AoT2CoT and CoT ablations with the same back end; gain grows with training scale. AoT responses are longer.
limits: Requires fine-tuning, which we cannot do. Longer outputs cost more tokens.
agent_relevance: Evidence that abstract-first order matters, transferable to us only as a prompt format.

source: Lewis & Mitchell (2024) Using Counterfactual Tasks to Evaluate the Generality of Analogical Reasoning in LLMs
finding: On letter-string analogies with altered alphabets, humans stay high while GPT models fall sharply. Contra Webb et al. (2023), GPT models were below humans even on the standard alphabet here.
numbers: 136 human participants (Prolific); 3 GPT models; 70 samples per cell for GPT vs 100 in Webb et al.; 40 symbol-alphabet problems. Human accuracy significantly above every GPT model on all alphabet types.
limits: Older GPT models; prompt format from Hodel & West worked best.
agent_relevance: A failed replication and boundary: apparent abstraction can be training-data similarity. Test our agent on counterfactual variants.

source: Wu et al. (2024) Reasoning or Reciting? Counterfactual Tasks
finding: On 11 tasks, GPT-4, GPT-3.5, Claude and PaLM-2 do above chance on counterfactual rule variants, but accuracy consistently and substantially falls versus default rules.
numbers: 11 tasks (arithmetic in other bases, chord playing and others). Zero-shot CoT usually helped but hurt PaLM-2 base-10 and base-16 addition and GPT chord playing.
limits: Comprehension checks show models often understand the rule yet fail to apply it.
agent_relevance: A good category label does not guarantee transfer. Verify by running (G3).

source: Moskvichev et al. (2023) The ConceptARC Benchmark
finding: 16 concept groups test abstraction and generalisation. Humans were far ahead of top ARC programs and GPT-4.
numbers: Humans over 90% average on 11 of 16 concepts and over 80% on the other 5. First-place Kaggle program below 60% on 11 of 16; second-place never reached 60%. GPT-4 below 30% on 15 of 16 concepts. Average human vs first-place gap 40 points.
limits: GPT-4 tested text-only; later reasoning models not covered.
agent_relevance: Our ARC portfolio: abstraction by concept, not by surface grid, is the open gap.

source: Sclar et al. (2024) Quantifying Language Models' Sensitivity to Spurious Features in Prompt Design
finding: Meaning-preserving formatting changes move accuracy by large amounts, not removed by scale, few-shot count or instruction tuning.
numbers: Up to 76 accuracy points for LLaMA-2-13B; about 10 points on average across 50+ tasks and several models.
limits: 2023 open-source models; format-level, not problem-level surface features.
agent_relevance: Representation fragility has a prompt-format part; fix the format and test several forms.

source: Larkin, McDermott, Simon & Simon (1980) Expert and novice performance in solving physics problems, Science
finding: Recalled, not opened: experts work forward from principles with physics-level representations; novices work backward with equation search. Written as production-system models.
numbers: None extracted this session.
limits: Recalled from memory only; verify before citing.
agent_relevance: Early computational model of the contrast; novice mode (means-ends over equations) is a baseline for plain LLM behaviour.

source: Chi, Feltovich & Glaser (1981) Categorization and representation of physics problems by experts and novices, Cognitive Science
finding: Recalled, not opened here: experts sorted by principle (energy conservation, Newton's second law), novices by surface objects (inclined planes, springs). Covered in the angle A file.
numbers: Exact N and percentages are in the angle A file; not re-extracted here.
limits: Small samples of advanced students vs undergraduates; recalled only.
agent_relevance: Defines the contrast we test machines against.

source: Bhaskar & Simon (1977) Problem solving in semantically rich domains: an example from engineering thermodynamics, Cognitive Science
finding: Recalled, not opened: a program (SAPA) solved textbook thermodynamics problems using domain schemas. An early schema-based representation system in AI.
numbers: None extracted.
limits: Recalled from memory only.
agent_relevance: Old system fitting S2 plus operator choice by problem class.

source: Forbus, Gentner & Law (1995) MAC/FAC: a model of similarity-based retrieval, Cognitive Science
finding: Recalled, not opened: two-stage retrieval, a cheap surface match first (MAC), then costly structure mapping on the shortlist (FAC). Predicts surface-biased retrieval. Covered in another subfield (analogical retrieval).
numbers: None extracted.
limits: Recalled from memory only.
agent_relevance: Embedding retrieval in LLM loops is the MAC stage; structure needs an explicit extra step.

source: Synthesis across the papers opened here: what prompt scaffolds change
finding: The scaffolds that help share one move: make the model state structure (principle, skill, type, relevant quantities) before computing. Gains range from small (RE2) to large (skill exemplars, step-back on weak baselines).
numbers: RE2 +1.2 to +5.3 points; skill exemplars +11.6 (MATH); step-back +15.1 (GPT-4 MMLU Physics 69.4 to 84.5) but CoT alone +13.5 there.
limits: Different baselines, models and seeds; not a controlled comparison.
agent_relevance: Ranking for S2: skill or principle labels and retrieval by label, then principle statement, then ignore-irrelevant instruction, then rephrase; re-reading is weakest.

source: Synthesis: failure families that bound LLM representation
finding: Three failure families recur: distractors (GSM-IC, GSM-NoOp), counterfactual rules (letter strings, Wu et al.), and format change (Sclar). Each shows keying to surface similarity with training data.
numbers: GSM-NoOp up to 65% drop; Sclar up to 76 points; Lewis & Mitchell: human curve flat, GPT curve falls.
limits: Mostly pre-2025 models; reasoning models narrow but do not remove the gap (o1-preview still -17.5% on NoOp).
agent_relevance: Test plan: score S2 on distractor, counterfactual and reformatted variants, not only clean items.

source: Gap in this angle: no direct LLM replication of Chi-style card sorting found
finding: Web search budget was used up and arXiv, OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar APIs returned 429 in this session, so no paper that has LLMs sort physics problems by principle vs surface was found or ruled out.
numbers: 0 direct hits (search failed; not a negative result).
limits: Absence of evidence only; retry when quota returns.
agent_relevance: Cheap own experiment: have a model sort 24 physics problems and compare with the Chi expert and novice groups.
